holding: uhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, J. The petitioner namely Taimoor Sattar was tried by the Trial Court for committing murder of his own father and mother namely Abdul Sattar deceased and Shamim Sattar deceased and vide judgment dated 06.04.2011, the Trial Court convicted the petitioner under section 302 (b) PPC and sentenced him to death on two counts with direction to pay compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the legal heirs of deceased on each count u/s 544-A Cr.P.C. or in default thereof to further undergo six months on each count. Being dissatisfied, the petitioner preferred appeal before the Lahore High Court, Lahore which was although dismissed vide impugned judgment dated 07.10.2015, however his sentence of death on two counts was converted into imprisonment for life on each count and benefit of section 382-B Cr.P.C. was extended to him. Bs. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 10.02.2010, within the precincts of the family’s residence, the petitioner allegedly bludgeoned his father, Abdul Sattar, and his mother, Mst. Shamim Sattar, to death using a hammer (Hathori). The motive attributed to this heinous act was JH No. 575/2018 @ thf petitioner’s resentment over his father’s refusal to transfer property inJhis name. 3] Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and having perused the entire record with their able assistance, we have irlcorporated and addressed the submissions and contentions raised dpring the course of arguments throughout the ensuing discussion and ahalysis within this judgment, thereby avoiding unnecessary repetition. . The grim facts of the prosecution case, as they emerge from the record, involve a rare and distressing instance of patricide and matricide. Ine case of prosecution rests on extra judicial confession, medical idence coupled with recoveries as well as forensic evidence and ifoulpatory statement made by the petitioner in his statement recorded nder section 342 Cr.P.C. We have observed that the matter has been eported with promptitude and the parties are already known to each ther therefore there is no probability of either manipulation or isidentification. It evinces from the record that the complainant Zafar qbal (PW-13) stated in his examination in chief that the petitioner made xtra judicial confession before him two times i.e. firstly on the phone nd secondly in presence of Muhammad Rafique Sajid (PW-10) when the etitioner was fleeing the place of occurrence in the car. No previous lenmity or adverse interest of these witnesses has been brought on record to impeach their character. The testimony of both the said witnesses seems reliable and confidence aspiring as their accounts regarding the material facts narrated have remained consistent and unimpeached despite rigorous cross-examination. The mode and manner of commission of offence as narrated finds significant accord with the medical evidence provided by Dr. Mansora Mirza (PW-7) and Dr. Fakhar- uz-Zaman (PW-8). The crush injuries to the skulls of both deceased persons described by PW-7 and PW-8 showing that the injuries were caused by blunt means, perfectly align with the nature of the weapon recovered. The recovery of weapon of offence (hathori) and blood stained clothes of petitioner from his bedroom on his own pointation further substantiate the prosecution story. The forensic evidence provides that the blood stained earth, weapon of offence (hathori) as well as the blood stained clothes contained human blood. In addition to this, the post occurrence conduct of petitioner is also not natural and his unexplained abscondence for ten days is also another circumstance which points LPINo, 575/2018 2 towards his involvement in this unfortunate occurrence. It does not appeal to a prudent mind that a person whose parents have been done to de4th in such a brutal manner would remain silent or remain absconded for|ten days without reporting such incident to police. We are well aware of the settled principle that in case of circumstantial evidence, every cirfumstance should be linked with each other and it should form such a comttinuous chain that its one end touches the dead body and the other thd neck of the accused. Similarly, if any link in the chain is missing thdn its benefit must go to the accused. We are also aware of the settled pripciple regarding extra judicial confession that such confession is regarded as a weak type of evidence, and utmost care and caution has to be Jexercised in placing reliance on such confession, In the instant case, thd petitioner was the last seen person leaving the crime scene who abg$conded for ten days without any explanation. He is the one who made false and contradictory statements to the employer of Abdul Sattar de¢eased and his uncle/complainant and later made extra judicial confession upon insistence. He is the person who disclosed the place where weapon of offence and his blood stained clothes were concealed anfi subsequently the same were discovered on his pointation. 5. Another crucial aspect in the instant case is the inculpatory stdtement of the petitioner recorded under section 342 of Cr.P.C. which is [perfectly in line with the other prosecution evidence. The law with regpect to inculpatory statements recorded in the statement of accused unler section 342 Cr.P.C. is settled that such statement has to be ac¢epted or rejected in its entirety and where prosecution's evidence was found to be reliable and the exculpatory part of such statement was esiablished to be false and excluded from consideration, then the indulpatory part of such statement might be read in support of prosecution's evidence.! Similarly, it is also trite law that the statement of|an accused recorded under section 342, Cr.P.C. is more reliable as compared to the judicial confession recorded under section 164, Cr.P.C.? The reason appears to be that there is less probability of duress or cofrcion and the accused is fully aware of the entire evidence recorded aghinst him as the former is recorded before the trial court after the witnesses for the prosecution have been examined and before the actused is called on for his defence whereas the latter is recorded during 1 Abhar Iqbal v. State (2013 SCMR 383) 2 SIR MEHMOOD Versus The STATE (2015 SCMR 423) investigation when the accused is in police custody. In the instant case thq petitioner categorically made an inculpatory statement and admitted to have committed the murder of his parents through the hammer i.e. in th¢ same mode and manner as established through other prosecution evidence. Similarly, the petitioner neither took any defence plea nor made any other exculpatory statement rather he admitted commission of offence in clear words. Keeping in view all the material, we have no doubt to] hold that all the circumstances are linked symmetrically pointing towards one and only conclusion of the guilt of the petitioner. 6 Regarding quantum of sentence, the petitioner failed to d¢émonstrate any mitigating circumstance which could enable this court td take a lenient view. The cold-blooded murder of his own defenseless pprents who raised him in such a callous manner, within the secure premises of their own house, is an aggravating circumstance which larrants a severe penalty. This atrocious act of parricide goes against the moral and social fabric of the society and, if not discouraged, has the lotential of destroying the family life of a large number of people. For this son, we have unanimously decided that the sentences of imprisonment for life of the petitioner shall run consecutively. ‘ For what has been discussed above, we do not find any legitimate round to interfere with the well-reasoned impugned judgment passed by e High Court. Furthermore, the impugned judgment does not suffer rom any non-reading or misreading of evidence. Thus, upon an overall eview of the available record, the petition being without merits is ismissed and leave refused, however the sentences of imprisonment for ife on two counts shall run consecutively. ISLAMABAD 11.05.2026 (Aqib Aman RO) Approved For Reporting
